channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: The only Belgian victim of the terrorist attacks on 11 September 2001
item.description: On 11 September 2001, the United States witnessed its worst terrorist attacks as multiple planes crashed into buildings on its East Coast.

item.title: Several dead in tour bus accident in Switzerland
item.description: Several people are reported dead following a road disaster involving a coach carrying Dutch tourists in Graubünden, eastern Switzerland.

item.title: August 2026 was the warmest month worldwide since records began
item.description: When oil, gas, or coal is burned, CO2 is released into the air, and this gas traps heat.

item.title: New high-speed train now connects Brussels Airport and major European city – with more to come
item.description: The ambition is to develop more international high-speed rail connections to better link Belgium to major European destinations.

item.title: They are 'gambling with our lives': AI researcher leaves Anthropic
item.description: British AI researcher leaves Anthropic, accusing AI companies of 'playing with our lives' in their race to build AI systems capable of improving themselves.

item.title: European gas price peaks at just over €80
item.description: Since the start of the Iran war in the Middle East, gas prices have more than doubled.

item.title: New night train connects Brussels and Milan from now
item.description: The train will run three times a week in each direction.

item.title: Explosives found at German power plant near Belgian border
item.description: Emergency services were sent out to investigate loud bangs and flashes of light near the high-voltage lines of the plant.

item.title: Ariane 6 could be adapted for manned flights, its designer says
item.description: As Europe rethinks its reliance on the USA in space exploration, ArianeGroup's CEO. says the Ariane 6 rocket launcher could be adapted for crewed flights.

item.title: Copper prices reach record high
item.description: The benchmark three-month copper futures contract rises by 0.8% to $14,533 a tonne, surpassing the previous record, set in January.

item.title: Nuclear reactor found in Syria could likely have be used to produce weapons - IAEA head
item.description: The former Syrian regime was building a nuclear reactor that could likely have been used to produce weapons-grade material, IAEA Director-General says.

item.title: 'Democracy is at risk': Americans in Belgium urged to post midterm ballots ahead of 19 September deadline
item.description: Ballots must be sent 45 days before election day, meaning 19 September this year.

item.title: FIFA president primed to stay in power despite scandals
item.description: The re-election push remains on even as Europe prepares criminal proceedings in Switzerland and searches for a rival, with no clear challenger yet in sight.

item.title: Russian foreign minister fears 'real war' after German accusations
item.description: An explosive-laden drone was found near a Ukrainian cargo aircraft, failed to detonate, and led Berlin to accuse Russian intelligence weeks later.

item.title: Ursula von der Leyen visits Greenland in show of support
item.description: Home to just 57,000 people, Greenland has become a geopolitical fault line. The EU visit underlines a push for investment, critical minerals and closer alignment with Europe over the US.

item.title: Belgian men arrested after violent scenes in Amsterdam
item.description: Several Belgians have been arrested after a shooting in Amsterdam on Monday night, which killed a man and left two police officers wounded.

item.title: Spain seizes control of Ceuta border
item.description: Madrid has authorised a temporary camp for migrants in Ceuta after an unprecedented 72,000 crossings in the space of a few days in July.

item.title: Thousands take to streets ahead of crucial German elections
item.description: Thousands protested for democracy on the streets of Magdeburg ahead of tomorrow's statewide elections, where the far-right AfD party is a clear frontrunner.

item.title: Moscow bombs Kyiv airport ahead of American visit
item.description: The details of the damage are still unknown. Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, two US envoys, are travelling to Ukraine this weekend.

item.title: Over 1,000 Europeans infected by West Nile virus
item.description: Most of the cases so far have been identified in Southern and Western European countries. The virus is spread mainly through mosquito bites.
